what: The fixture set the regression harness (eval/regress.py) and the other cycle agents' claims rest on. Audio is never committed (*.wav is git-ignored); this file says how to regenerate each fixture and what a number measured on it can and cannot support. Regenerate with `python3 eval/fixtures.py generate --out DIR`; check with `python3 eval/fixtures.py verify DIR`.
determinism: sha256 values were measured on macOS 26.6.2 with the say voices installed on the Mac mini M2 Pro of the cycle, by generating twice and comparing: identical. A different macOS release or voice build changes the audio but not the reference structure; `verify` then reports a mismatch as a WARNING (the fixture still works for A/B, but the numbers are not comparable with earlier ones).

say-synthetic-taglish.same_as: eval/make-synthetic.sh (the two commands, into a scratch directory instead of eval/audio)

supports: A/B comparison of two builds on identical audio (WER, RTF, collapse, live counters)
cannot_support: any claim about real Taglish accuracy (an Indonesian say voice reading Taglish; wrong acoustics)
real meeting behaviour: no overlap, no noise, no turn-taking
live commit latency at a natural pause: its sub-700 ms gaps never fire the silence boundary

supports: live utterance finalization and boundary commits (1.2 s of silence after every punctuated word, 26 pauses)
A/B of live commit latency with a pause boundary available
cannot_support: real pause behaviour: pauses are digital silence and exactly 1.2 s
WER comparisons with the unpaused clip: same reference, different audio

supports: DER A/B of two diarizer builds: two clearly different voices, the easy case
cannot_support: real-meeting DER: text-to-speech voices, exact boundaries, no crosstalk

supports: DER A/B on the FINDINGS 10 case: two similar voices trading short turns inside shared 10 s chunks
cannot_support: a claim that a diarizer separates similar real people; no method may split this pair

supports: DER A/B on separable voices trading short turns (the FINDINGS 10 mechanism without the unsplittable pair)
DER A/B where chunk-level embeddings fuse two separable voices
DER A/B with three speakers and one-word backchannels
DER A/B with four speakers, a longer file
DER A/B with low overlap: a backchannel starts before the previous turn ends

external.source: google/fleurs, fil_ph, test split, on Hugging Face
external.expected_layout: FLEURS_DIR/test.tsv plus FLEURS_DIR/test/test/*.wav (the layout the Taglish agent downloaded to /tmp/notero-data/fleurs)
external.selection: the K clips whose sha1(file name) sorts first, concatenated in that order with 0.5 s of silence between; reference = the tsv's normalized transcript column, joined

expected_when_present.note: for the FLEURS fil_ph test split as downloaded on 2026-11-01; the harness records the actual hashes in each report, it does not enforce these

supports: A/B regression of read-speech Tagalog accuracy on public data, identical audio for both builds
cannot_support: any claim about Taglish or code-switching (FLEURS Filipino is read, monolingual-ish sentences)
meeting speech: single speakers reading, studio-ish conditions
absolute WER: the concatenation changes VAD and windowing against per-clip decoding
